results.evidence: No source states a 60 m rope. One high-route account lists 'a 30m rope may be useful'; a Mountaineers report on the East Col climbed on 40 m rope teams; the Mountaineers report that describes two single-rope rappels to the saddle gives no rope length. Per-rappel lengths are unknown, so no two sources agree on a length to adopt.

results.fact: How the summit section is descended
results.evidence: One Mountaineers party made two single-rope rappels back to the saddle and downclimbed the rest; another party (2023 blog) left a bail anchor of nuts and a sling at the 4th-class notch step rather than downclimb a 5.8 move; another party made a careful roped descent of class 3-4 rock. Parties handle it differently and it is not established whether the 'saddle' of the rappel report is the ~7,500 ft notch, so the conflicting descriptions cannot be reconciled to one line from sources.

results.fact: Location and rock quality of the crux
results.evidence: A 2023 account puts a 4th-class step on poor rock below a notch near 7,500 ft, with a clear class 3 gully above to good summit-block rock. Another account (east face line) roped a short Class 4 slot in a crumbly breccia cliff band low above the col, then scree, then a nice Class 4 dihedral and class 3 ledges near the top; a third calls it a 4th-class scramble from the notch to the summit. The accounts follow different lines, so no two agree on where the crux sits.

results.fact: Elevation of the Mystery Glacier foot
results.evidence: A Mountaineers route description has parties drop from 6,200 ft camps in Deception Basin to about 6,000 ft to reach the glacier, which is then climbed to the ~6,700 ft col at its upper right. Row-internal: climbing_route[0], pitch_detail[2] and beta all have the party DESCEND from the ~6,560 ft divide into Deception Basin before climbing the glacier to a 6,700 ft col, so a 6,650 ft terminus is impossible; USGS 3DEP ground at the terminus pin itself reads ~5,810 ft and the basin floor around it 5,700-5,900 ft.
